beats.intent: Four boxes in a row and five dots above them
beats.narration: Five pigeons and only four holes.
beats.code:
stage.title("The pigeonhole principle")
holes = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=1.2, color=BLUE) for _ in range(4)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3).shift(DOWN)
birds = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.14, color=YELLOW) for _ in range(5)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5).shift(UP * 1.8)
stage.play(Create(holes), FadeIn(birds))
stage.add(holes, birds)

beats.intent: Four dots dropped one into each box
beats.narration: Put one pigeon in each hole: four are placed.
beats.code: stage.play(*[birds[k].animate.move_to(holes[k]) for k in range(4)], run_time=1.2)

beats.intent: The fifth dot dropped into a box that already has one, that box lit red
beats.narration: The fifth has to share. Some hole must hold at least two.
beats.code:
stage.play(birds[4].animate.move_to(holes[2].get_center() + RIGHT * 0.3))
highlight(stage, holes[2], color=RED)
stage.caption("5 into 4: some box gets 2")

request: how many squares are there on a chessboard?

beats.intent: An 8 by 8 grid of squares
beats.narration: A chessboard has sixty four small squares, but there are bigger squares too.
beats.code:
stage.title("Squares on a chessboard")
board = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.45, color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.6 if (i + j) % 2 else 0.1) for i in range(8) for j in range(8)]).arrange_in_grid(8, 8, buff=0)
stage.play(FadeIn(board))
stage.add(board)

beats.intent: A 2 by 2 square and a 3 by 3 square outlined on the board
beats.narration: A two by two square can sit in seven by seven places; a three by three in six by six.
beats.code:
two = Square(side_length=0.9, color=YELLOW).move_to(board[0].get_center() + np.array([0.225, -0.225, 0]))
three = Square(side_length=1.35, color=RED).move_to(board[27].get_center() + np.array([0.45, -0.45, 0]))
stage.play(Create(two), Create(three))
stage.add(two, three)

beats.intent: Bars of the counts 64, 49, 36, 25, 16, 9, 4, 1 for sizes 1 to 8
beats.narration: Every size k fits in nine minus k squared places: sixty four, forty nine, down to one.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
bars = draw_bars(stage, [64, 49, 36, 25, 16, 9, 4, 1], labels=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8])
stage.equation(r"1^2 + 2^2 + \cdots + 8^2 = 204")

request: why is the total of all the handshakes' degrees always even?

beats.intent: A network of five people with six friendships
beats.narration: Five people and who is friends with whom.
beats.code:
stage.title("The handshake lemma")
nodes = {"A": (-0.8, 0.4), "B": (0, 0.8), "C": (0.8, 0.4), "D": (0.5, -0.6), "E": (-0.5, -0.6)}
edges = [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "A"), ("A", "C")]
dots, lines = draw_network(stage, nodes, edges)

beats.intent: Each node labelled with its number of friends: 3, 2, 3, 2, 2
beats.narration: Count each person's friends: three, two, three, two, two.
beats.code:
for n, d in (("A", 3), ("B", 2), ("C", 3), ("D", 2), ("E", 2)):
    stage.label(dots[n], str(d), direction=DOWN, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The network beside 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 12 = 2 × 6
beats.narration: They add to twelve, twice the six friendships, because every friendship has two ends.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"3 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 12 = 2 \times 6")

request: does V - E + F = 2 work for a cube?

beats.intent: A cube drawn flat as two squares joined at their corners
beats.narration: Draw a cube as a front square, a back square and the edges joining them.

beats.intent: The 8 corners lit, then the 12 edges
beats.narration: It has eight corners and twelve edges.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, VGroup(*dots.values()), color=YELLOW)
highlight(stage, VGroup(*lines), color=GREEN)
stage.caption("V = 8, E = 12")

beats.intent: The cube beside 8 - 12 + 6 = 2
beats.narration: And six faces. Eight minus twelve plus six is two, as for every polyhedron without holes.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"V - E + F = 8 - 12 + 6 = 2")

request: how do you count people in two overlapping groups?

beats.intent: Two overlapping circles: 12 people play football, 9 play tennis
beats.narration: Twelve people play football and nine play tennis.
beats.code:
stage.title("Inclusion–exclusion")
A = Circle(radius=1.8, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.2).shift(LEFT * 1)
B = Circle(radius=1.8, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.2).shift(RIGHT * 1)
stage.play(Create(A), Create(B))
stage.add(A, B)
stage.label(A, "football 12", direction=UP, color=BLUE)
stage.label(B, "tennis 9", direction=UP, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: The overlap shaded with the 4 who play both
beats.narration: Four of them play both, so they sit in the overlap.
beats.code:
lens = Intersection(A, B, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.6)
stage.play(FadeIn(lens))
stage.add(lens)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("4", font_size=36).move_to(lens)))

beats.intent: The circles beside 12 + 9 - 4 = 17
beats.narration: Adding twelve and nine counts those four twice, so take them off once: seventeen people.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"|A \cup B| = 12 + 9 - 4 = 17")

request: how does voltage split in a series circuit?

beats.intent: A battery of 12 V and three resistors in a loop drawn as boxes
beats.narration: A twelve volt battery drives current through three resistors in a row: two, four and six ohms.
beats.code:
stage.title("A series circuit")
loop = Rectangle(width=7, height=3.2, color=GREY_B)
bat = Rectangle(width=0.4, height=1, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=1).move_to(loop.get_left())
rs = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=1, height=0.4, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to(loop.get_top() + RIGHT * x) for x in (-2, 0, 2)])
stage.play(Create(loop), FadeIn(bat), FadeIn(rs))
stage.add(loop, bat, rs)
stage.label(bat, "12 V", direction=LEFT, color=YELLOW)
for r, v in zip(rs, ("2 Ω", "4 Ω", "6 Ω")):
    stage.label(r, v, direction=UP)

beats.intent: Bars of the voltage across each resistor: 2, 4 and 6 volts
beats.narration: The same one amp flows through all of them, so each takes voltage in proportion to its resistance.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
bars = draw_bars(stage, [2, 4, 6], labels=["2 Ω", "4 Ω", "6 Ω"])

beats.intent: The bars beside 2 + 4 + 6 = 12 V
beats.narration: Two, four and six volts: together, the battery's twelve.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"I = \frac{12}{2 + 4 + 6} = 1\ \text{A}", r"2 + 4 + 6 = 12\ \text{V}")

request: why do the diagonals of a rectangle cut each other in half?

beats.intent: A rectangle with corners (0,0), (4,0), (4,2), (0,2) on a grid
beats.narration: Take a four by two rectangle.

stage.title("Diagonals of a rectangle")
p = draw_plane(stage, x_extent=5, y_extent=3)
rect = Polygon(p.c2p(0, 0), p.c2p(4, 0), p.c2p(4, 2), p.c2p(0, 2), color=BLUE)
stage.play(Create(rect))
stage.add(rect)

beats.intent: Both diagonals drawn, crossing at (2, 1)
beats.narration: Draw both diagonals. They cross at two, one.
beats.code:
d1 = draw_line(stage, p.c2p(0, 0), p.c2p(4, 2), color=YELLOW)
d2 = draw_line(stage, p.c2p(0, 2), p.c2p(4, 0), color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The four half-diagonals marked equal, each √5 long
beats.narration: Two, one is the midpoint of each diagonal, so they cut each other exactly in half.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\text{midpoint} = \left(\tfrac{0+4}{2}, \tfrac{0+2}{2}\right) = (2, 1)")

request: why is the area of a kite half the product of its diagonals?

beats.intent: A kite with diagonals 4 and 6
beats.narration: A kite with diagonals four and six.
beats.code:
stage.title("Area of a kite")
kite = Polygon([0, 3, 0], [2, 1, 0], [0, -3, 0], [-2, 1, 0], color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.8)
d1 = DashedLine(kite.get_vertices()[0], kite.get_vertices()[2], color=WHITE)
d2 = DashedLine(kite.get_vertices()[3], kite.get_vertices()[1], color=WHITE)
stage.play(Create(kite), Create(d1), Create(d2))
stage.add(kite, d1, d2)

beats.intent: A 4 by 6 rectangle drawn around the kite
beats.narration: Draw the rectangle around it, four wide and six tall: the diagonals are its width and height.
beats.code:
box = Rectangle(width=4 * 0.8, height=6 * 0.8, color=YELLOW).move_to(kite.get_center())
stage.play(Create(box))
stage.add(box)
stage.caption("The kite fills exactly half the box")

beats.intent: The four outside triangles matching the four inside ones, beside Area = ½ × 4 × 6 = 12
beats.narration: Each outside triangle is a copy of one inside, so the kite is half the box: half of its diagonals multiplied.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\text{Area} = \tfrac12 \, d_1 d_2 = \tfrac12 \times 4 \times 6 = 12")

request: how does a truth table for AND and OR work?

beats.intent: Two inputs A and B listed in four rows: 00, 01, 10, 11
beats.narration: Two switches, A and B, each off or on: four combinations.
beats.code:
stage.title("AND and OR")
rows = [(0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1)]
cell = lambda v, c: VGroup(Square(side_length=0.7, color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.6 if v else 0.05).set_fill(c if v else BLACK), Text(str(v), font_size=26))
table = VGroup(*[VGroup(cell(a, BLUE), cell(b, BLUE)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0) for a, b in rows]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0).shift(LEFT * 2)
stage.play(FadeIn(table))
stage.add(table)

beats.intent: An AND column added: only the last row is 1
beats.narration: AND is on only when both are on: just the last row.
beats.code:
andc = VGroup(*[cell(a & b, GREEN) for a, b in rows]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0).next_to(table, RIGHT, buff=0.4)
stage.play(FadeIn(andc))
stage.add(andc)
stage.label(andc, "AND", direction=UP, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: An OR column added: every row but the first is 1
beats.narration: OR is on when either is on: every row except the first.
beats.code:
orc = VGroup(*[cell(a | b, YELLOW) for a, b in rows]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0).next_to(andc, RIGHT, buff=0.4)
stage.play(FadeIn(orc))
stage.add(orc)
stage.label(orc, "OR", direction=UP, color=YELLOW)
